issues.description: The problem statement claims the environment's printf expects two parameters on the stack (first the string length, then the string pointer), but both the template and the solution push only a single parameter (the string pointer) and adjust the stack by 4 bytes (add esp, 4). This is a cross-artifact parameter/stack convention mismatch that can confuse students about how to call printf and how much stack space to clean up (should be 4 vs. 8).
issues.suggested_fix: Either update the problem statement to remove or correct the incorrect hint about printf expecting two parameters (reflecting that the provided template/solution use a single pointer parameter and clean up 4 bytes), or modify the template and solution to actually push both parameters (push length; push pointer) and adjust the stack cleanup to add esp, 8. The simpler fix (and least disruptive to the exercise) is to correct the problem statement so it matches the code in the template/solution.
